Every option at its default, as shipped on rev-245.2.

# examples/full-config-reference.yaml
# =============================================================================
# goscape — FULL CONFIGURATION REFERENCE
# =============================================================================
# This file documents EVERY configuration key the server understands, each set
# to its built-in default. It is a reference, not a starter config: copy only
# the keys you want to override into your own file. For a minimal working
# preset, see examples/bundled/goscape.yaml.
#
# This file is itself a valid config. Verify it without starting the server:
#   go run ./cmd/goscape --config.file examples/full-config-reference.yaml --config.verify=true
#
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# How configuration is resolved (lowest to highest precedence):
#   1. built-in defaults (the values shown below)
#   2. this config file            (--config.file <path>)
#   3. environment variables       (only when expansion is enabled, see below)
#   4. CLI flags                   (e.g. --world.tcp-listen-port 43594)
#
# Strictness: the loader uses strict YAML decoding. An UNKNOWN key is a fatal
# boot error, not a warning — keep keys exactly as spelled here.
#
# Meta-flags (value flags — the `=true` is required; the bare form errors):
#   --config.file=<path>        config file to load
#   --config.verify=true        validate config and exit (no server start)
#   --config.expand-env=true    expand ${VAR} / $VAR in this file from the
#                               environment before parsing
#
# Env-var expansion: with --config.expand-env=true, any ${VAR} in a value is
# replaced by the environment. Example: dsn: ${GOSCAPE_DB:-data/goscape.db}
#
# NOTE: every value below is the built-in DEFAULT, with one exception — the four
# module `enable:` keys are set to `true` so this file is a coherent "run
# everything" config (the code default for each is `false`). A module runs only
# when BOTH its `enable:` is true AND it is included by the active `target`.
# =============================================================================


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Global settings (top level)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Which module(s) to run. The selected target pulls in its dependencies.
#   ondemand  HTTP OnDemand server only
#   world     TCP game server only
#   login     gRPC login service only
#   friends   friends server only
#   all       run everything (default)
# CLI: --target
target: all

# Minimum severity to log. One of: trace | debug | info | warn | error.
# CLI: --log.level   (default: info)
log_level: info

# Log output format. One of: text | json.
# CLI: --log.format   (default: text)
log_format: text

# How the `source` attribute is rendered. One of:
#   relative  module-root-relative path, e.g. modules/world/npc_masks.go:42
#             (stays clickable from the repo root in an IDE) — default
#   short     filename only, e.g. npc_masks.go:42
#   full      the compiler's path: absolute under a plain `go run`, or
#             import-path-rooted under -trimpath builds
# CLI: --log.source   (default: relative)
log_source: relative


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ondemand — HTTP OnDemand server (serves the client cache + /rs2.cgi bootstrap,
#            optional WebSocket -> world bridge)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ondemand:
  # Run the ondemand module. Code default: false. (yaml-only; no CLI flag.)
  enable: true

  # --- HTTP listener (inlined dskit server.Config) ---
  # CLI: --ondemand.http-listen-network (default: tcp)
  http_listen_network: tcp
  # CLI: --ondemand.http-listen-address (default: 127.0.0.1)
  http_listen_address: 127.0.0.1
  # CLI: --ondemand.http-listen-port (default: 8080)
  http_listen_port: 8080

  # --- HTTP server timeouts (inlined dskit server.Config) ---
  # CLI: --ondemand.graceful-shutdown-timeout (default: 30s)
  graceful_shutdown_timeout: 30s
  # CLI: --ondemand.http-read-timeout (default: 30s)
  http_server_read_timeout: 30s
  # CLI: --ondemand.http-write-timeout (default: 30s)
  http_server_write_timeout: 30s
  # CLI: --ondemand.http-idle-timeout (default: 120s)
  http_server_idle_timeout: 120s

  # --- Source-IP logging (inlined dskit server.Config) ---
  # CLI: --ondemand.log-source-ips-enabled (default: true)
  log_source_ips_enabled: true
  # Header to read the client IP from. Default mirrors the TS getIp() primary.
  # Setting a custom header REPLACES (not augments) dskit's built-in
  # Forwarded / X-Real-IP / X-Forwarded-For chain. Blank both header and regex
  # to fall back to that chain.
  # CLI: --ondemand.log-source-ips-header (default: cf-connecting-ip)
  log_source_ips_header: cf-connecting-ip
  # Regex whose first capture group is the IP. Default extracts the first
  # comma-separated address (TS .split(',')[0].trim()).
  # CLI: --ondemand.log-source-ips-regex
  log_source_ips_regex: '^\s*([^,]+?)\s*(?:,|$)'
  # Log all matched source IPs instead of only the first.
  # CLI: --ondemand.log-source-ips-full (default: false)
  log_source_ips_full: false

  # --- Static-file + cache serving ---
  # Directory with main_file_cache.dat + idx0..4; archive-0 files are served
  # over HTTP from here. CLI: --ondemand.cache-path (default: ./data/pack)
  cache_path: ./data/pack
  # Directory served as a static-file fallback after named routes miss.
  # CLI: --ondemand.public-dir (default: ./public)
  public_dir: ./public

  # --- /rs2.cgi bootstrap params (mirror the world module's NODE_* values;
  #     keep these in sync with the world module when running both) ---
  # CLI: --ondemand.node-id (default: 10)
  node_id: 10
  # CLI: --ondemand.node-members (default: true)
  node_members: true
  # World TCP port; rs2.cgi emits portoff = node_port - 43594 to the applet.
  # CLI: --ondemand.node-port (default: 43594)
  node_port: 43594
  # Whether rs2.cgi may serve the Java applet template when plugin=1.
  # CLI: --ondemand.node-debug (default: true)
  node_debug: true

  # --- WebSocket -> world bridge ---
  websocket:
    # Serve a WS bridge at "/" that forwards binary frames to the world module's
    # TCP connection handler. CLI: --ondemand.websocket-enable (default: true)
    enable: true
    # Explicit Origin allowlist. Empty => allow all (TS default). Non-empty =>
    # the Origin header must exactly match an entry or the upgrade is rejected.
    # (yaml-only; no CLI flag.)
    allowed_origins: []
    # Max size of a single inbound WS message, in bytes.
    # CLI: --ondemand.websocket-max-payload-bytes (default: 2000)
    max_payload_bytes: 2000
    # Mirror of TS NODE_WS_ONDEMAND: permit WS-originated connections to enter
    # the OnDemand (state-2) path. NOTE: not enforced at the proxy layer today
    # (see PORTING.md rev244-b3-ws-ondemand-gate); recorded for parity.
    # CLI: --ondemand.websocket-ws-ondemand (default: false)
    ws_ondemand: false

  # Inject a per-deployment token cookie into the rs2.cgi client page. When
  # true, pub_pem (below) MUST be set and parse as an RSA public key.
  # CLI: --ondemand.websocket-token-protection (default: false)
  ws_token_protection: false
  # RSA public key (PKIX PEM bytes) used to derive the per-deployment token when
  # ws_token_protection is true. yaml-only; omit unless you enable protection.
  #pub_pem: |
  #  -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
  #  ...
  #  -----END PUBLIC KEY-----

  # --- Advanced dskit server.Config knobs (inlined; no CLI flag; rarely set) ---
  # Per-module log level override (yaml-only; no CLI flag); falls back to the
  # top-level log_level. Valid levels: debug, info, warn, error.
  # (ondemand inherits the dskit HTTP server layer, which does not support trace.)
  #log_level: info
  # HTTP server read-header timeout (default: 0 = no separate header timeout).
  #http_server_read_header_timeout: 0s
  # Log connections closed before any response was written.
  #http_log_closed_connections_without_response_enabled: false
  # Request-header logging / level / exclusions.
  #log_request_headers: false
  #log_request_at_info_level_enabled: false
  #log_request_exclude_headers_list: ""
  # Strip this prefix from incoming request paths before routing.
  #http_path_prefix: ""


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# database — central database shared by login + friends (independent clients)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Central database shared by the login and friends services. Both are
# independent clients of it — with the sqlite backend they must share a
# filesystem; postgres lifts that to a network database, letting login and
# friends run on separate hosts against one database.
database:
  # Backend: sqlite | postgres.
  backend: sqlite
  sqlite:
    # SQLite file path (parent directories are created automatically).
    dsn: data/goscape.db
  postgres:
    # PostgreSQL DSN, e.g. postgres://user:pass@host:5432/goscape?sslmode=disable
    # Required when backend=postgres.
    dsn: ""
    # Max open connections per service pool.
    max_open_conns: 8


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# friends — gRPC friends / private-message server
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
friends:
  # Run the friends module. CLI: --friends.enable (code default: false)
  enable: true
  # CLI: --friends.grpc-listen-address (default: 127.0.0.1)
  grpc_listen_address: 127.0.0.1
  # CLI: --friends.grpc-listen-port (default: 2005)
  grpc_listen_port: 2005
  # Per-world player slot cap. CLI: --friends.world-player-limit (default: 2000)
  world_player_limit: 2000
  # CLI: --friends.graceful-shutdown-timeout (default: 30s)
  graceful_shutdown_timeout: 30s
  # Per-module log level override (yaml-only; no CLI flag); falls back to the
  # top-level log_level. Valid levels: trace, debug, info, warn, error.
  #log_level: info


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# login — gRPC login service (account store + player saves; central database,
#         see database: above)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
login:
  # Run the login module. CLI: --login.enable (code default: false)
  enable: true
  # CLI: --login.grpc-listen-address (default: 127.0.0.1)
  grpc_listen_address: 127.0.0.1
  # CLI: --login.grpc-listen-port (default: 2004)
  grpc_listen_port: 2004
  # Player save-file root directory. CLI: --login.save-path (default: data/players)
  save_path: data/players
  # bcrypt work factor for password hashing (valid 4..31).
  # CLI: --login.bcrypt-cost (default: 10)
  bcrypt_cost: 10
  # Profile name used in DB queries. CLI: --login.node-profile (default: main)
  node_profile: main
  # Create accounts on first login. CLI: --login.auto-register (default: true)
  auto_register: true
  # Upgrade non-members to members on member worlds.
  # CLI: --login.auto-subscribe-members (default: true)
  auto_subscribe_members: true
  # CLI: --login.graceful-shutdown-timeout (default: 30s)
  graceful_shutdown_timeout: 30s
  # Per-module log level override (yaml-only; no CLI flag); falls back to the
  # top-level log_level. Valid levels: trace, debug, info, warn, error.
  #log_level: info


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# world — TCP game server (the engine)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
world:
  # Run the world module. (yaml-only; no CLI flag. Code default: false.)
  enable: true

  # --- TCP listener ---
  # CLI: --world.tcp-listen-network (default: tcp)
  tcp_listen_network: tcp
  # CLI: --world.tcp-listen-address (default: 127.0.0.1)
  tcp_listen_address: 127.0.0.1
  # CLI: --world.tcp-listen-port (default: 43594; valid 1..65535)
  tcp_listen_port: 43594

  # --- TCP timeouts ---
  # CLI: --world.tcp-read-timeout (default: 30s)
  tcp_server_read_timeout: 30s
  # CLI: --world.tcp-write-timeout (default: 2s; per-flush budget on tick goroutine)
  tcp_server_write_timeout: 2s
  # CLI: --world.tcp-idle-timeout (default: 120s)
  tcp_server_idle_timeout: 120s
  # TCP keepalive idle period before the first probe; 0 disables.
  # CLI: --world.tcp-keepalive-period (default: 30s)
  tcp_keepalive_period: 30s
  # CLI: --world.graceful-shutdown-timeout (default: 30s)
  graceful_shutdown_timeout: 30s

  # --- Cache / content ---
  # Cache root; gamemap loads map-pack files from <path>/maps/.
  # CLI: --world.cache-path (default: ./data/pack)
  cache_path: ./data/pack
  # Source content root that enables ::rebuild's in-process PackAll and the midi
  # name->id registry. Empty disables the cheat.
  # CLI: --world.content-path (default: "")
  content_path: ""
  # Watch content_path subdirs and auto-::rebuild on change (debounced 1s).
  # Requires content_path to be set. CLI: --world.content-watch (default: false)
  content_watch: false
  # Optional PEM RSA private key (PKCS#1/PKCS#8) to decrypt the login block,
  # replacing the built-in default key. The Java client must carry the matching
  # public key. Empty uses the built-in key.
  # CLI: --world.rsa-private-key-path (default: "")
  rsa_private_key_path: ""

  # --- Inter-module connections ---
  # CLI: --world.login-server-address (default: 127.0.0.1:2004)
  login_server_address: 127.0.0.1:2004
  # CLI: --world.login-server-enabled (default: true)
  login_server_enabled: true
  # CLI: --world.friends-server-address (default: 127.0.0.1:2005)
  friends_server_address: 127.0.0.1:2005
  # Connect to the friends server. CLI: --world.friends-server-enabled
  # (default: false; the bundled example sets this true to use the friends module)
  friends_server_enabled: false

  # --- Node / gameplay settings (mirror TS Environment NODE_*) ---
  # World ID, offset by 9. CLI: --world.node-id (default: 10)
  node_id: 10
  # Whether members content is available. CLI: --world.node-members (default: true)
  node_members: true
  # Auto-upgrade accounts that log into this world to members.
  # CLI: --world.node-auto-subscribe-members (default: true)
  node_auto_subscribe_members: true
  # addxp multiplier. CLI: --world.node-xp-rate (default: 1)
  node_xp_rate: 1
  # Max live NPCs. CLI: --world.node-max-npcs (default: 8191)
  node_max_npcs: 8191
  # Max connected clients. CLI: --world.node-max-connected (default: 1000)
  node_max_connected: 1000
  # WalkTrigger dispatch mode: 0=PLAYERPACKET (default), 1=PLAYERSETUP,
  # 2=PLAYERMOVEMENT. CLI: --world.node-walk-trigger-setting (default: 0)
  node_walktrigger_setting: 0
  # Min wealth value for the wealth event. CLI: --world.node-minimum-wealth-value-event (default: 10)
  node_minimum_wealth_value_event: 10
  # Run in production mode. CLI: --world.node-production (default: false)
  node_production: false
  # --- Client input-tracking ---
  # Whether clients are instructed to submit detailed input-tracking events.
  # CLI: --world.node-submit-input (default: false)
  node_submit_input: false
  # Max approximate bytes per single input-tracking session.
  # CLI: --world.node-limit-bytes-per-tracking-session (default: 50000)
  node_limit_bytes_per_tracking_session: 50000

  # --- Debug / dev ---
  # Extra debug info (e.g. missing triggers). CLI: --world.node-debug (default: true)
  node_debug: true
  # Client-side route finding. CLI: --world.node-client-route-finder (default: true)
  node_client_routefinder: true
  # Prefix char for ::debugproc cheats. CLI: --world.node-debugproc-char (default: ~)
  node_debugproc_char: '~'
  # Profile name. CLI: --world.node-profile (default: main)
  node_profile: main
  # CLI: --world.node-debug-profile (default: false)
  node_debug_profile: false
  # CLI: --world.node-debug-socket (default: false)
  node_debug_socket: false

  # --- Advanced / rarely set ---
  # Per-module log level override (yaml-only; no CLI flag); falls back to the
  # top-level log_level. Valid levels: trace, debug, info, warn, error.
  #log_level: info
  # TCP read-header timeout (yaml-only; default: 0 = none).
  #tcp_server_read_header_timeout: 0s

  # --- Deprecated / unused (accepted but read by no live code path) ---
  # Unused: nothing reads this field; the player cap is hardcoded (newPlayerList(2048)).
  #node_max_players: 2047
  # Declared but consumed by no code path.
  #enable_tcp_server: false


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# NOT a config section: pkg/telemetry exists in the codebase but is NOT wired
# into the application config. There is no top-level `telemetry:` block — adding
# one fails strict decoding. This is intentional, not a TODO:
#
#   - pkg/telemetry is a dormant emit seam. The engine calls
#     telemetry.Get().Emit*(...) in a few places (login, world, wealth), but the
#     default Emitter is a no-op and nothing in THIS build calls telemetry.Set()
#     or InitProviders() outside tests — so every event lands in the no-op sink.
#   - app.Config only aggregates configs for modules that run here, and there is
#     no telemetry module. No code path reads telemetry.Config to construct a
#     real Emitter, so a `telemetry:` block would configure nothing.
#   - A real Emitter / transport (OTLP, Kafka, …) is supplied out-of-tree; that
#     is where telemetry.Config is consumed. The public core keeps only the
#     interface, the call sites, and the pkg/eventspb schema.
#
# Wiring telemetry.Config in here would surface keys (kafka / otlp / …) that do
# nothing in this build — strictly worse under strict decoding than omitting it.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

items.title: single-binary-values.yaml
items.text:
---
# Run all four modules (ondemand + world + login + friends) in one StatefulSet.
deploymentMode: SingleBinary

singleBinary:
  replicas: 1
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
  extraEnv:
    - name: GOMEMLIMIT
      value: "900MiB"

persistence:
  enabled: true
  size: 5Gi

service:
  type: ClusterIP

---
# Central management: login + friends only (no world). Worlds dial this release.

persistence:
  enabled: true

goscape:
  node:
    id: 1
  # Point these at your Management release's Service (see its NOTES output):
  loginServerAddress: ""    # e.g. goscape-mgmt:2004
  friendsServerAddress: ""  # e.g. goscape-mgmt:2005

  replicas: 1

items.title: Porting Lessons (TypeScript → Go, RuneScape server)
items.text:
Cross-revision knowledge for porting a LostCityRS Engine-TS server revision to Go. This is the durable, repo-owned distillation of what makes these ports correct and what bites if you translate naively. Read it before starting a new revision.

Companion files: REFERENCES.md (pinned upstream commits per revision), and each revision branch's own README.md / CLAUDE.md / PORTING.md / docs/PORTING-CLOSED.md (revision-specific conventions and the deviation tracker).

items.title: 1. Philosophy
items.text:
Faithful 1:1 translation is the default. Every ported game-logic region maps to an identifiable Engine-TS function, cited inline as // TS <File>.ts:<lines>. goscape adapts the infrastructure (dskit service lifecycle, module system, config layering) to Go idiom, but inside ported game logic do not refactor opportunistically — behaviour bugs are found by diff-checking the Go region against the cited TS source.

Byte-faithful at the boundaries. Wire protocol (ISAAC, RSA, opcodes), codecs (bzip2, CRC, wordenc), collision, and the pack pipeline's cache output are byte-for-byte against the reference. The pack pipeline is verified by byte-diffing script.dat (and friends) against the cache the upstream TS meta-repo packs.

Deviations are tracked, never silent. Each revision branch carries PORTING.md (active backlog) + docs/PORTING-CLOSED.md (closed rows, parity tables, audit history). Accepted in-code divergences carry a PORTING-EXCEPTION (<row-id>, <short>) marker — grep -rn "PORTING-EXCEPTION" modules pkg cmd internal lists every accepted exception (10 at the time of the multi-revision conversion).

items.title: 2. Porting workflow for a new revision
items.text:
The Go port of revision N is (Go port of revision N-1) + (the translated TS delta). That makes it a branch operation:

  1. Branch rev-N from the nearest prior Go revision branch (e.g. rev-225).
  2. Diff the primary TS reference across the gap. Look up the prior revision's pinned commit in REFERENCES.md, then git -C Engine-TS diff <prev-commit>..<new-commit>. That diff is your work list.
  3. Translate each TS change into the corresponding Go region, applying the gotcha rules in §3. The Go branch diff (git diff rev-(N-1) rev-N) should correspond change-for-change to the TS diff — this is your audit.
  4. Record the new reference commits in REFERENCES.md under ## rev-N — including the Content and RuneScriptTS pins, which move together with the engine (the pack byte-parity baseline shifts with all three).
  5. Each revision branch is self-contained (its own code, tooling, CI). Do not share code packages across revisions — independent faithful translations.
  6. Carry the tracker forward. PORTING.md rows that still apply travel with the branch; close rows using the closure shapes defined in PORTING.md §Tracking conventions (FIXED / EXCEPTION-DOCUMENTED / NO-DIVERGENCE / NOT-A-GAP).

items.title: 3. TS → Go translation gotchas
items.text: Each is a real bug class hit during the rev-225 port. Verify against the TS source before "fixing" anything that merely looks wrong — and before preserving anything that merely looks intentional.

items.title: Identity & operand encoding
items.text:
• Pick ONE identity per subsystem. Player identity exists as both uid and protocol slot; mixing them inside one subsystem caused repeated bugs (e.g. an obj-ownership check keyed by uid everywhere except one network handler that used slot). Convention: the network layer speaks slot, world/script logic speaks uid.
  • Script int-operand encoding is bit-packed. The VARP/VARN secondary- player flag is bit 16 of the int operand ((intOperand>>16)&1), not a 0/1 selector. .-prefixed (secondary-player) script commands must use operand-aware accessors (activePlayer()), not Self, or writes silently hit the wrong player.

items.title: Shared-handler / fork drift
items.text:
• When N opcodes share one TS handler, Go shares one implementation. Forking per-opcode drifts (three move opcodes → one TS MoveClickHandler; the Go fork forgot modal-close in one copy). Parameterize the wire delta, not the behaviour.
  • When TS keeps logic in a shared base class (PathingEntity), a fix must land in BOTH Go forks (Player and Npc) — Go has no inheritance, so the shared TS line exists twice.
  • Two parallel compute paths can feed the same wire field. Fix the path that actually serializes (the renderer read accessors, not the bridge-fed struct field) — the spawn-orientation bug was "fixed" twice on the wrong path first.

items.title: Tick order & scheduling
items.text:
• Tick ORDER is behaviour. TS interleaves movement between pre-step and post-step interaction passes; running "movement, then interactions" broke walk-up combat. Port the pipeline order, not just the pieces.
  • Player.Save() is tick-goroutine-only. Off-tick paths (disconnect, shutdown) must route through the relay action queue so saves run on-tick; three separate save-loss paths came from violating this.
  • The protected-access invariant is load-bearing for content. All ~1159 .rs2 content scripts consume items after a dialogue yield without checking inv_del's return. That is safe ONLY because runScript refuses to start a protected script while another holds protected access (TS Player.ts:2094). Immediate-run handlers (the opheld family, if_button / inv_button) bypass CanAccess() and rely solely on that guard; script resumes bypass runScript entirely (the force=true path). Removing or weakening the guard re-opens live item-dupe exploits.

items.title: Trust nothing that isn't the TS source
items.text:
• A test can pin a bug. A "deviation" test that contradicts TS may be enshrining the bug it was written around — verify against TS before preserving the pinned contract, and update the test when TS disagrees.
  • "By design" / "handled elsewhere" comments lie. A comment claiming a divergence is intentional (or covered by another path) is the prime suspect, not evidence. Re-verify against TS before trusting it.
  • Ask "what does TS do?" FIRST. Before estimating any gap as implementation work, check the TS state: if TS itself has the feature stubbed or commented out (NpcMode QUEUE1..20), the correct Go closure is documentation, not implementation.
  • Mis-described audit rows are themselves misdirection. Severity or category in a finding can be wrong; re-derive the divergence claim from first principles against current TS + Go before acting on it.

items.title: Pack pipeline / byte parity
items.text:
• Fix determinism FIRST, then byte-diff. A "non-deterministic output" complaint against an external baseline can hide a multi-bug stack: one map-iteration-order bug masked four separate parity bugs that only became visible once output was stable. Go map iteration is randomized — any ordered output derived from a map needs explicit ordering.
  • Mirror TS's data-driven dispatch. Discriminating types via Go pointer equality (instead of the data-driven check TS does) is fragile and broke default-value emission.
  • jagFileVersion=26. Do not bump to 27 unless the upstream meta-repo pins @lostcityrs/runescript past 750291c (see REFERENCES.md).

items.title: Process
items.text:
• Capture go test's real exit code — and stress-run any fix that changes RNG-dependent behaviour. A flaky test passing once by RNG luck masked a real regression.
  • Get a live client debug log EARLY when headless repros keep passing — one tick-ordering bug was invisible to every synthetic repro and obvious in the first live log.

items.title: 4. Comment & reference conventions
items.text:
• Cite TS by file and line: // TS World.ts:128-129 next to the ported region. The file/symbol is the durable anchor; line numbers drift — fix them when touching the code, don't invest in keeping them precise.
  • No per-comment revision tags. The branch is the revision context, and REFERENCES.md pins the exact TS commit — together they make every bare // TS: comment unambiguous.
  • PORTING-EXCEPTION (<row-id>, <short>) one-line markers (with a See PORTING.md cross-reference) index every accepted divergence in code. Keep them grep-discoverable; each keeps its row-id reference.
  • PORTING.md is updated as a side effect of any work that touches a tracked region; closed rows move to docs/PORTING-CLOSED.md.

items.title: 5. Verification
items.text:
• Gates: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./..., and go test -race on touched packages (the race detector needs CGO_ENABLED=1, the default). The world tick loop is goroutine-heavy; race coverage matters.
  • Byte parity: ISAAC, RSA, opcodes, bzip2, CRC, wordenc, and collision are byte-faithful and pinned by tests; pack output is byte-diffed against the upstream-packed cache when the pack pipeline changes.
  • Pin tests: when a fix lands, pin the TS-correct contract with a test. When an existing test pinned the buggy contract, update the test — after verifying against TS (§3, "A test can pin a bug").

items.title: Future revisions
items.text:
When porting revision N:

  1. Add a ## rev-N section below recording the reference commits used.
  2. Branch the Go code rev-N from rev-225 (or the nearest prior revision).
  3. Diff the primary reference across the gap — git -C Engine-TS diff e1dea19f..<rev-N commit> — and apply the corresponding Go deltas on the rev-N branch, so the Go branch diff mirrors the TS revision diff.
  4. Bump the Content and compiler pins in the same section (the compiler is revision-dependent: RuneScriptTS for 225, RuneScriptKt for 244+) — the pack pipeline is byte-parity-checked against the cache the upstream packs, so engine, content, and compiler move together.

items.title: RuneScript
items.text:
RuneScript is the domain-specific scripting language used by the LostCity RuneScape engine (and historically by Jagex's RS2/RuneScape revisions) to drive content: NPC dialogue, item interactions, quests, combat AI, interface logic, and timed behavior. Scripts are stored as .rs2 source, compiled to a stack-based bytecode, and executed by a per-engine ScriptRunner against a ScriptState.

This document captures the language as it appears in the LostCityRS/Content corpus and as the goscape engine ports it from LostCityRS/Engine-TS.

items.title: 1. File layout & triggers
items.text:
A .rs2 file contains one or more scripts, each introduced by a bracketed trigger header of the form [trigger,subject]. The trigger names the event that fires the script; the subject names the entity (or interface component, or queue slot) it binds to.

[opheld1,bronze_dagger]
mes("You inspect the dagger.");

[oploc1,oak_tree]
mes("You swing your axe at the oak.");

[opnpc1,man]
chatnpc("Hello there.");

Common trigger families:

Family Examples Fires when… Inventory item ops opheld1..opheld5, opheldu, opheldt Player clicks an option on an inv item Loc (scenery) ops oploc1..oploc5, oplocu, oploct, aploc1..aploc5 Player clicks a scenery option (ap = approach/out-of-range) NPC ops opnpc1..opnpc5, opnpcu, opnpct, apnpc* Player clicks an NPC option Ground obj ops opobj1..opobj5, opobju, opobjt Player clicks a ground item Player ops opplayer1..opplayer5 Player right-clicks another player AI ai_queue1..ai_queue20, ai_timer, ai_spawn, ai_aprange NPC behaviour ticks Queues / timers queue,name, weakqueue,name, timer,name Engine drains the named queue / timer Lifecycle login, logout, autocon Per-player session events Interface if_button,iface:comp, if_buttond, inv_button UI interactions on an open interface Code-only proc,name, label,name, debugproc,name Called from other scripts Client-side clientscript,name Compiled into the client cache

[proc,...] scripts return values and are invoked via ~name(args); [label,...] scripts are invoked via jump @name(args) and never return.

items.title: 2. Variables
items.text:
RuneScript has four variable scopes, each disambiguated by sigil:

Sigil Scope Lifetime $x Script-local One script execution %x Player varp / vartemp / varbit Per-player (varp persisted, vartemp wiped on logout) ^x Constant Compile-time ~x Procedure call (not a variable, but same family) n/a

Locals are typed at declaration:

def_int $count = 0;
def_string $name = "Bob";
def_obj $weapon = null;
def_coord $home = 0_50_50_25_25;

Varp writes go through engine setters; the apparent no-op %score = %score still emits a real OpVarpSmall packet (PUSH_VARP + POP_VARP) so the client re-runs cs1 listeners on that varp — useful for forcing a UI resync.

Constants live in .constant files and are inlined at compile time:

^max_hp_level    99
^bank_iface      12

items.title: 3. Types
items.text:
Primitive: int, string, boolean (encoded as int 0/1), coord.

Cache-typed references are first-class; the compiler verifies the symbol exists in the corresponding config:

obj, namedobj, loc, npc, seq (anim), spotanim, synth (sound), stat, inv (inventory id), enum, struct, param, dbtable, dbrow, dbcolumn, interface, component, category, mapelement.

null is the universal absent-value, type-narrowed by context.

A coord literal packs level_mx_mz_lx_lz:

def_coord $lumby = 0_50_50_25_25;   // level 0, map (50,50), local (25,25)

items.title: 4. Expressions & control flow
items.text:
Arithmetic uses infix calc(...); outside calc only assignments and calls are syntactically permitted on the right-hand side:

$total = calc($base + $bonus * 2);
$dmg   = calc(random(^max_hit) + 1);

Conditionals use C-style if / else if / else with =, !, <, >, <=, >=, & (and), | (or):

if ($hp < calc(%maxhp / 4)) {
    mes("You are badly wounded.");
} else if ($hp < calc(%maxhp / 2)) {
    mes("You are wounded.");
}

Loops are while (...):

$i = 0;
while ($i < inv_size(inv)) {
    if (inv_getobj(inv, $i) = coins) {
        $found = true;
    }
    $i = calc($i + 1);
}

switch_int, switch_obj, switch_npc, etc. are typed jump tables:

switch_int ($choice) {
    case 1 : mes("First.");
    case 2,3 : mes("Second or third.");
    case default : mes("Other.");
}

items.title: 5. Procedures, labels, and the call stack
items.text:
A proc is a typed function with declared params and return tuple:

[proc,greet](string $who)(string)
return("Hello, " + $who + "!");

[opnpc1,man]
def_string $line = ~greet("traveller");
chatnpc($line);

A label is tail-called: control transfers and never returns. Labels are how long-running NPC AI cycles are written without growing the call stack.

gosub is the dynamic dispatch form (gosub("name", args)). When a gosub'd script suspends (e.g. on delay), the caller's frame parks; the engine resumes it on a later tick. In the goscape port, callers are responsible for flipping Execution = Running before resuming — TS does this in ScriptRunner; goscape leaves it explicit, which is an easy invariant to miss.

items.title: 6. Pointers (the implicit active* register)
items.text:
RuneScript's runtime carries a small set of active pointers — a player, an npc, a loc, an obj, etc. — that most commands implicitly consume. Triggers set the relevant pointers on entry: [opheld1,...] arrives with active player and active obj; [opnpc1,...] arrives with active player and active npc.

Many commands have a primary form (acts on the active player) and a .npc suffixed form (acts on the active npc):

anim          // animates active player
npc_anim      // animates active npc
stat          // reads active player stat
npc_stat      // reads active npc stat

The bytecode verifier enforces that the requisite pointer is set; a script that calls npc_anim without an active npc fails at compile time.

items.title: 7. Queues, timers, and engine-driven scheduling
items.text:
Four queue flavours, all triggered via [queue,name] / [ai_queue,name]:

Command Survives logout? Survives death? Use case queue no no Tick-delayed action weakqueue no no Cancellable scenery animation longqueue yes yes Persistent quest beat strongqueue no yes (engine drops on death) Combat hits, must-fire effects

weakQueue is the cancellable cohort; queue.all() and weakQueue.all() are walked separately each tick (two distinct loops, ten lines apart in TS — easy to miss when porting).

settimer(timer_id, interval, args...) registers a recurring trigger that fires every interval ticks until cleartimer is called.

STRONGQUEUE and LONGQUEUE are variadic opcodes — they take a script ID plus an arbitrary number of int/string arguments. They do not share helper shape with fixed-arg siblings; porting them as fixed-arg silently breaks.

items.title: 8. Dialogue & string formatting
items.text:
chatnpc(string) and chatplayer(string) open a chat dialogue; mes(string) prints to the message box; objbox(obj, string) shows an item dialogue.

The chatnpc/chatplayer family uses | (pipe) as the line-break delimiter — the engine SPLIT_INITs on | and renders one line per segment. <br> works in mes but not in chat dialogue.

Inline tags:

<col=ff0000>red text</col>
<shad=000000>shadowed</shad>
<u>underline</u>
<str>strikethrough</str>
<img=N>            // sprite
<gt> <lt>          // literal > and <

tostring(int) converts; string_length(s), substring(s, start, end), uppercase(s), lowercase(s), parahelper(s, n) manipulate.

// Movement / location
p_walk, p_telejump, p_teleport, p_arrivedelay

// Inventory

// Stats

// Animation / FX

// NPCs

npc_queue, npc_settimer, npc_findhero, npc_damage, npc_heal

// Locs / ground objs
loc_add, loc_del, loc_change, loc_anim,
obj_add, obj_del, obj_count, obj_takeitem

// Interfaces

// Math / RNG

// Queues / timers / control

gosub, jump, return

items.title: 10. Engine-side notes (goscape porting)
items.text:
A few places where RuneScript semantics constrain the engine implementation:

  • %X = %X is not a no-op. It compiles to PUSH_VARP then POP_VARP, which writes through to the client packet stream and re-runs the client's cs1 listeners on that varp. Clients short-circuit on equal-value writes; the server cannot.
  • No [varp,X] content trigger exists in the LostCity engine — varp changes drive client UI directly and cannot be hooked content-side. Bugs that look "varp-driven" must be fixed engine-side or via the writing site.
  • Suspended gosubs defer to later ticks. A npc_death script that gosubs into a delay'd subroutine pauses; test fixtures must drive n.turn per tick to resolve the cascade.
  • Iterator commands (npc_findall, loc_findall, obj_findall, etc.) use a single-tick template: a custom iterator struct, a state field on the ScriptState, a lazy snapshot built from Lookup.ZoneFoo, and a staleness check on access.
  • ScriptArgument[] is a sum type in TS. goscape splits it into parallel intArgs []int + stringArgs []string slices; opcodes that take mixed types must thread both.

items.title: 11. A worked example
items.text:
A small NPC quest-giver: greet, branch on quest stage, deliver a reward.

[opnpc1,quest_man]
if (%quest_stage = 0) {
    chatnpc("Will you help me find my missing cat?|"
          + "Last seen near the old well.");
    %quest_stage = 1;
} else if (%quest_stage = 1) {
    if (inv_total(inv, missing_cat) > 0) {
        chatnpc("My cat! Thank you, traveller.");
        inv_del(inv, missing_cat, 1);
        ~give_reward();
        %quest_stage = 2;
    } else {
        chatnpc("Have you found my cat yet?");
    }
} else {
    chatnpc("Thanks again for finding my cat.");
}

[proc,give_reward]()
inv_add(inv, coins, 100);
stat_advance(thieving, 250);
mes("<col=ff8800>You receive 100 coins and some XP.</col>");
